\[
\hat{R} = \frac{\sum_{q \in W} e^{-K C_I^2 d_q}\, I_q}{\sum_{q \in W} e^{-K C_I^2 d_q}}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(d_q\): The distance of pixel q from the center
- \(C_I\): The coefficient of variation of the window
- \(K\): The damping

d_q is the distance of window pixel q from the center, and C_I the coefficient of variation of the window. In flat areas C_I is small, the weights are nearly equal, and the output is close to the window mean. Near edges C_I is large, the weights fall off fast, and the output stays close to the pixel. This is the exponential weighting of Frost and others, with the damping K, as it is usually implemented.
